title: Carbon monoxide, methane and carbon dioxide columns retrieved from SCIAMACHY by WFM-DOAS: year 2003 initial data set
abstract: Abstract. The near-infrared nadir spectra measured by SCIAMACHY on-board ENVISAT contain information on the vertical columns of important atmospheric trace gases such as carbon monoxide (CO), methane (CH4), and carbon dioxide (CO2). The scientific algorithm WFM-DOAS has been used to retrieve this information. For CH4 and CO2 also column averaged mixing ratios (XCH4 and XCO2) have been determined by simultaneous measurements of the dry air mass. All available spectra of the year 2003 have been processed. We describe the algorithm versions used to generate the data (v0.4; for methane also v0.41) and show comparisons of monthly averaged data over land with global measurements (CO from MOPITT) and models (for CH4 and CO2). We show that elevated concentrations of CO resulting from biomass burning have been detected in reasonable agreement with MOPITT. The measured XCH4 is enhanced over India, south-east Asia, and central Africa in September/October 2003 in line with model simulations, where they result from surface sources of methane such as rice fields and wetlands. The CO2 measurements over the Northern Hemisphere show the lowest mixing ratios around July in qualitative agreement with model simulations indicating that the large scale pattern of CO2 uptake by the growing vegetation can be detected with SCIAMACHY. We also identified potential problems such as a too low inter-hemispheric gradient for CO, a time dependent bias of the methane columns on the order of a few percent, and a few percent too high CO2 over parts of the Sahara.
problem: High-quality trace gas column retrieval from SCIAMACHY near-infrared spectra is challenging due to instrument calibration issues, including high dark signals and a detector ice layer causing time-dependent errors, and the difficulty of detecting weak absorption lines against a noisy background.
method: This paper proposes a method to correct time-dependent bias in methane retrievals by applying a daily scaling factor derived from measurements over the Sahara and normalizing the methane columns by simultaneously retrieved carbon dioxide columns.
task: The task is to retrieve vertical columns of carbon monoxide, methane, and carbon dioxide from SCIAMACHY satellite spectra for 2003 using the WFM-DOAS algorithm and to evaluate this initial data set by comparing it with global measurements and models.
innovation: This paper presents the first year-long (2003) dataset of carbon monoxide, methane, and carbon dioxide columns retrieved from SCIAMACHY satellite measurements using the WFM-DOAS algorithm, providing an initial validation that shows the data can identify major sources and sinks like biomass burning and vegetation uptake.

In the following we present a detailed comparison of the retrieved XCO2 with TM3 model simulations. TM3 3.8 (Heimann and Körner, 2003) is a three-dimensional global atmospheric transport model for an arbitrary number of active or passive tracers.
In this case, TM3 was run with a resolution of 1.8×1.8 deg and 28 layers, and the meteorology fields were derived from the NCEP/DOE AMIP-II reanalysis.

Recently (May 2005), we have reprocessed the year 2003 data for CO and XCH4 with a new version (v0.5) of the WFM-DOAS retrieval algorithm. Our initial analysis indicates that at least some of the major problems identified for the v0.4x data products discussed in this paper have been solved.
For example, the v0.5 CO is retrieved from an optimized fitting window and is not scaled any more (the v0.4 product was scaled with the factor 0.5).
For v0.5 XCH4 the methane column is obtained from channel 6 which is not affected by the ice issue.
